title: What If Dark Matter Vanished From the Universe?

scenes.text: What if dark matter vanished tonight? Every galaxy would lose most of the gravity holding it together.
It makes up about 85 percent of all matter in the universe, roughly five times more than everything we can see.
Astronomers found it because stars move too fast. The visible matter alone cannot keep them in orbit.
Every galaxy sits inside a halo of it. Take the halo away, and the pull on the outer stars falls sharply.
By that math, galaxies would no longer stay bound. Their outer stars would drift off into empty space.
You would not notice tonight, because galaxies turn very slowly. But the invisible glue holding them together would be gone.

description:
What if dark matter vanished from the universe?
It makes up about 85 percent of all matter, and without its gravity galaxies could not stay bound.
What should we run through next?
